findings.issue_text: [BUG] useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable calls ctx.hasPermissionInMetadata(...) but ctx is not among the imports in useAbilities.ts (the diff's import block pulls in useFolder, AccessControlAction, alertmanagerApi, etc. — no ctx), so this module does not compile. TypeScript/webpack build fails with 'Cannot find name ctx' for every consumer of useAbilities.ts, including AlertRuleMenu and RuleActionsButtons.V2; the PR cannot build at all unless ctx is imported somewhere not shown.

[BUG] useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities calls useGrafanaRulesSilenceSupport() and useCanSilenceInFolder(rule?.folderUid), but neither hook is imported in the diff's import section and neither name appears elsewhere in the codebase's existing abilities module (only useCanSilence is used previously). If these hooks are not added in a non-diff file, the build fails with 'Cannot find name useGrafanaRulesSilenceSupport' / 'useCanSilenceInFolder'; the new silence-permission path in the rule-list menu is dead on arrival.

[BUG] The diff imports isProvisionedPromRule and isProvisionedRule from '../utils/rules', but isProvisionedPromRule is not shown being defined anywhere in this diff and does not exist in the pre-diff utils/rules (which only had isProvisionedRule per RuleActionsButtons.tsx usage). Unless isProvisionedPromRule is added to utils/rules in a file outside this diff, both useAbilities.ts and RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx fail to compile with a missing-export error.

[BUG] The test asserts editButton href contains `/alerting/${rule1.grafana_alert.uid}/edit`, but RuleActionsButtons.V2 builds the URL as `/alerting/${encodeURIComponent(ruleId.stringifyIdentifier(identifier))}/edit` where the identifier is a GrafanaRuleIdentifier whose stringified form includes the rule source name (e.g. 'grafana/<uid>'), so the produced href is percent-encoded and will not contain the asserted substring. These two assertions fail when the test suite runs; the component's actual edit URL format and the test's expectation were never reconciled, meaning the tests as written do not pass against the shipped code.

[ADVISORY] GrafanaRuleListItem reads `rule?.isPaused` from GrafanaPromRuleDTO, but the old GrafanaRuleListItem sourced pause state from the ruler DTO's `is_paused` field with `rule?.isPaused ?? is_paused`, indicating the Prometheus DTO may not carry a camelCase isPaused field. If GrafanaPromRuleDTO lacks isPaused, this is a compile error; if it exists but is never populated by the prom rules endpoint, paused rules silently render as unpaused in the new list view.

[BUG] useAllRulerRuleAbilities hardcodes isFederated = false (replacing the isFederatedRuleGroup check), so federated rule groups lose their immutable classification and become editable/deletable For a federated rule group in a Mimir-backed datasource, immutableRule is now false, so the menu renders Delete/Duplicate/Update for rules the previous code blocked; a user can attempt to delete a rule they do not own, and the test coverage for federated behavior (previously exercised via isFederatedRuleGroup in the deleted combined-rule path) was removed with no replacement

[BUG] GrafanaGroupLoader silently drops the transitional Creating and Deleting rule states: rules present only in the ruler API (Creating) or only in the prom API (Deleting) are no longer rendered because the ruler query and matchRules matching were removed entirely During rule create/delete propagation, users see the rule vanish from the list (Deleting) or not appear at all (Creating) instead of seeing the transitional status icon the list previously displayed; the deleted tests 'should render rule with url and creating state when only ruler rule exists' and 'should render delete rule operation list item when only prom rule exists' confirm these were acceptance criteria that are now unimplemented and untested

[BUG] GrafanaRuleListItem drops the returnTo query parameter from the rule view link that GrafanaRuleLoader's item included via createReturnTo() Users navigating from the filtered rule list to a rule detail page lose their 'back to list' return context that the old item restored via href: createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo }); no test in the diff asserts the href query params

[ADVISORY] The dual-path OR logic (ruler ability OR grafana ability) in AlertRuleMenu is never exercised against real hook implementations — every test in the diff mocks useRulerRuleAbilities/useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, so the combination semantics (e.g. ruler path reporting unsupported while grafana path allows) are unverified A regression in the OR combination or in one hook's supported/allowed flags for the same action would pass CI; the RulesTable tests assert only per-hook mock return values, not that AlertRuleMenu derives the correct visible actions from both paths

[ADVISORY] GrafanaRuleListItem accepts an operation prop but the only remaining caller (GrafanaGroupLoader) never passes it, and the Creating/Deleting operation rendering paths it forwards to AlertRuleListItem are now unreachable Dead prop surface invites confusion: the next maintainer wiring a transitional state will assume GrafanaRuleListItem supports it (it forwards it correctly) while the data pipeline that produced those states was deleted, making the change harder to reason about

[ADVISORY] useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable returns loading:false when !rule || !folderUID, conflating 'rule not loaded yet' with 'checked and not editable' — during the initial render before the prom rule/folder arrives, abilities report NotSupported-with-allowed=false, then flip to allowed on the next render Consumers that make one-shot decisions from the first render (or tests asserting the settled state on an early frame) see action buttons/menu items flicker or briefly hidden; the loading flag the older useIsRuleEditable path exposed for this case is swallowed

[ADVISORY] GrafanaGroupLoader no longer checks the query error state of useGetGrafanaGroupsQuery; an error response yields data undefined and falls into the generic 'cannot fetch rules' Alert, losing the RulerRuleLoadingError-style error detail the deleted GrafanaRuleLoader path surfaced Operators debugging a failing Grafana prom rules endpoint see only a generic error alert with no underlying error surfaced in the group slot, where previously rule-level load errors carried the error object

[BUG] useAllAlertRuleAbilities now hardcodes isFederated = false, dropping the previous isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) check, so federated rule groups lose their immutable protection Federated Grafana rules rendered via useAllAlertRuleAbilities no longer get Update/Delete suppressed by the immutableRule branch, so users are offered edit/delete/pause actions on rules they cannot actually modify through their owning group

[BUG] AlertRuleMenu ORs ruler-based abilities with Grafana-prom-folder-based abilities for ALL consumers, not just the list view, so two different permission systems are unioned everywhere the menu renders On the rule details view a user who lacks the ruler/datasource-level permission but holds folder-level permission now sees Pause/Delete/Export menu items that the previous single-source check correctly hid (or vice versa: menu items appear whose corresponding backend action will 403), a behavioral expansion not traceable to the stated 'list view no longer calls ruler API' intent

[BUG] Removing the ruler query and matchRules deletes the Creating/Deleting transitional-state rendering, so rules being created or deleted now render as normal active rule list items During the propagation window between ruler and Prometheus state, a newly created rule disappears from the list entirely (only prom rules are iterated) and a just-deleted rule shows as a healthy clickable rule, whereas the previous UI showed 'Creating'/'Deleting' status; the deleted tests explicitly covered these cases and were removed rather than migrated

[BUG] The new GrafanaRuleListItem drops the returnTo query parameter that the replaced GrafanaRuleListItem in GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx added to the rule href via createReturnTo() Users navigating from the list to a rule view lose the return-to-list breadcrumb behavior that existed in the old list path, a silent UX regression bundled into an abilities refactor

[ADVISORY] A custom `skipToken` Symbol is exported from useAbilities.ts, shadowing RTK Query's well-known skipToken concept with a different mechanism (undefined-swapping) inside the same codebase The next contributor will import skipToken from @reduxjs/toolkit/query (the conventional source) and pass it to these hooks; the hooks only check `rule === skipToken` against this local Symbol, so a foreign skipToken is treated as a real undefined rule by coincidence but any future hook checking token identity diverges — two 'skip' conventions coexist

[ADVISORY] RuleActionsButtons.V2 silently ORs ruler and grafana-prom edit abilities and additionally returns null (rendering nothing, including the delete/silence buttons previously available) whenever neither rulerRule nor a grafana promRule is provided For non-Grafana prom-only rules the component logs a warning and renders no action buttons at all, changing behavior for any existing caller that previously passed only promRule; the logWarning fires per rule row on the list page, generating warning noise at list scale

[ADVISORY] The RBAC test suite now maintains parallel mock implementations for useAlertRuleAbility, useRulerRuleAbility, useGrafanaPromRuleAbility, useRulerRuleAbilities and useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, duplicating the same permission logic five ways per test case Every future ability or action added requires updating five mock implementations per test; drift between the singular and plural mocks (already visible: the Delete test mocks useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities but not useGrafanaPromRuleAbility) means tests silently stop exercising the real component wiring

[BUG] useAllRulerRuleAbilities hardcodes isFederated = false (with a TODO), so federated rule groups are no longer treated as immutable and Pause/Delete/Update are offered for rules the previous code locked down. Users see and can trigger Edit/Delete/Pause menu actions on federated rule groups where those operations are invalid; the previous isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) check was dropped with no replacement, so the immutability invariant is silently unenforced.

[BUG] useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable calls useFolder(folderUID) for every GrafanaPromRuleDTO it is invoked on, and useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities is invoked per rule via useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities in AlertRuleMenu for every list row — an N+1 folder-fetch pattern on the rule list hot path. A list page with ~80 rules issues ~80 folder lookup hooks/requests (one per row) where the list previously made zero ruler-side permission fetches; this reintroduces the exact per-row request fan-out the PR's stated goal ('removed all requests to the ruler API in the list view') was meant to eliminate.

[BUG] Dropping the ruler API entirely removes both transitional state representations: ruler-only rules no longer render as 'Creating' and prom-only rules no longer render as 'Deleting' (matchRules and RuleOperationListItem paths deleted). A rule mid-creation or mid-deletion silently vanishes from the list until the next poll reconciles, instead of showing the Creating/Deleting state — a sentinel-meaning change: absence of a row that previously meant 'in transition' now means the rule appears to not exist at all.

[BUG] isPaused is now sourced only from rule?.isPaused, dropping the ruler-rule fallback (rule?.isPaused ?? is_paused) the deleted GrafanaRuleLoader used. If the Grafana prom rules endpoint does not populate isPaused for a paused rule (the field was previously sourced from the ruler DTO's grafana_alert.is_paused), paused rules render as unpaused in the list — a displayed-state mismatch versus the rule's real state.

[ADVISORY] Every ability is computed as rulerAbility OR grafanaPromAbility, creating two parallel permission-evaluation paths whose result is the union of their grants. Any future divergence between the ruler-side checks (useAllRulerRuleAbilities) and the prom-side checks (useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities — different helpers like useCanSilenceInFolder vs useCanSilence, getRulesPermissions('grafana') hardcoded) silently widens permissions to the more permissive path; the staff-level shape here is a single ability source per rule type, not an OR of two.

[ADVISORY] getIsProvisioned for the prom-rule path now depends on isProvisionedPromRule(promRule) reading provenance from the prom rules endpoint, replacing the previous ruler-side grafana_alert.provenance check — a single-source-of-truth swap with no verification the prom endpoint carries the field. If GrafanaPromRuleDTO omits or under-populates provenance (it was authoritative on the ruler DTO), provisioned rules are detected as unprovisioned and rendered editable — the exact immutability the provisioned check exists to protect.

[ADVISORY] The new GrafanaRuleListItem drops the returnTo parameter the deleted GrafanaRuleLoader passed to createRelativeUrl for the view href. Users navigating from the new rule list to a rule detail page lose 'return to list' behavior; the next developer touching hrefs has to re-discover why returnTo existed.

[ADVISORY] Leftover '// duplicate' comment on the useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable call, and the comment block about redundant per-rule calls was moved onto the deprecated hook while the new prom-rule hook reintroduces the same redundancy. The code now documents a known scalability problem in one hook while creating the identical shape in its successor, signaling the duplication between useAllRulerRuleAbilities and useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities will keep diverging (isFederated TODO exists only in one of them — observed drift already).

[BUG] The diff silently deletes the 'Creating' and 'Deleting' transitional-state rendering (matchRules, promOnlyRules, RuleOperation.Creating/Deleting items) from the rule list, replacing an accepted feature with happy-path-only behavior without any human acceptance of that scope change. During ruler→Prometheus propagation lag, users no longer see rules being created or deleted in the list view; rules that are mid-deletion disappear instantly and newly created rules never appear until Prometheus catches up, a silent regression of the state-indicator intent the previous tests explicitly asserted.

[BUG] Review iterations rewrote the test suite from state-transition coverage (ruler-only 'Creating', prom-only 'Deleting', matchRules unit tests) to permission/button happy-path tests, silently changing the objective the tests encode. The deleted tests were the only executable specification of the Creating/Deleting behavior and the matchRules matching algorithm; deleting them plus the implementation means no future reviewer can distinguish an intentional feature removal from an accidental regression.

[BUG] useAllRulerRuleAbilities hard-codes isFederated = false (with a TODO replacing the previous isFederatedRuleGroup call), silently removing the federated-rule immutability guarantee that the original code enforced. Users can now Edit/Delete/Pause rules inside federated rule groups, where edits do not propagate as intended, turning a previously blocked action into an allowed one without any recorded decision to drop that constraint.

[BUG] The new GrafanaRuleListItem drops the returnTo parameter from the view href that the deleted GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx implementation included (createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })). Users navigating from the list to a rule and using the browser back affordance no longer return to their filtered list position — a UX behavior silently lost in the rewrite with no test or changelog noting it.

[ADVISORY] The 'should render More button with action menu options' test replaced the 'creating state' test but asserts only that the More button exists — it no longer verifies the rule link/href behavior the original test covered. Coverage drift: the original test verified rule links and creating-state icons; the replacement verifies button presence only, so a regression in link generation or rule identity would pass CI unnoticed.

[ADVISORY] useAllAlertRuleAbilities was silently re-pointed from getRulesSourceName(rule.namespace.rulesSource) to getGroupOriginName(groupIdentifier.fromCombinedRule(rule)) while keeping its public signature, changing which data source name drives permission checks for existing callers. Out-of-tree or unmodified in-tree callers of the still-exported useAllAlertRuleAbilities now compute permissions from the group-origin name instead of the namespace's rules source; for non-grafana sources this can flip permission results, and the change is invisible at the call site because the hook signature is unchanged.

[ADVISORY] The refactor changes permission semantics from 'AND of ruler ability' to 'OR of ruler ability and grafana-prom ability' (canPause = (ruler && ruler) || (grafana && grafana)) without the component's consumers or the stated intent acknowledging the loosening. A rule that the ruler API says is unsupported but the prom path reports as allowed now shows actions that previously were hidden — e.g. plugin-provided or provisioned rules handled differently by the two ability paths may become editable/deletable in the menu, expanding what users can attempt beyond the original intent.

[ADVISORY] Authorization for edit is now the logical OR of two independently computed ability checks (ruler-based and promRule-based), so an action is offered whenever either path grants it rather than when the authoritative path does. The union composition is fail-open: whichever hook has the more permissive semantics wins. For Grafana-managed rules rendered from the list view (rule === undefined, promRule set), the promRule path in useAbilities.ts now hardcodes MaybeSupported = AlwaysSupported and checks only folder metadata permissions, dropping the ruler-availability and loading gating the ruler path enforced; a user whose folder metadata grants update but who is denied by any server-side rule-level condition the old path covered is shown an Edit/Delete button whose action the backend then rejects — UI-exposed authorization decided by the weaker of two checks rather than the server's actual policy.

[ADVISORY] useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities replaces the loading/isRulerAvailable support gate with unconditional AlwaysSupported, so Delete, Pause, Duplicate and Restore become 'supported' for every Grafana prom rule as soon as loading completes. Menu action availability (the [supported, allowed] pair) is no longer derived from any capability signal, only from folder metadata permissions; combined with the OR-union in AlertRuleMenu/RuleActionsButtons.V2 this means action buttons are rendered purely on client-side permission metadata for rules the ruler path would have marked unsupported, exposing mutation entry points (delete modal, clone flow, silence drawer) to users the previous gating hid — server enforcement is the only remaining barrier.

[ADVISORY] useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable authorizes edit/delete purely from the folderUid string carried in the API-returned GrafanaPromRuleDTO via ctx.hasPermissionInMetadata, with no validation that the rule actually resides in that folder. The permission decision is keyed on a server-supplied field that the diff treats as trusted input; any path that lets a rule be rendered with a mismatched or attacker-influenced folderUid (e.g. cross-folder rule rendering in the new list view) causes the folder's permission metadata to be evaluated for the wrong folder, granting edit/delete UI for a rule outside the user's authorized folder — the server rejects the write, but the authorization model now depends on an unscoped, response-controlled identifier rather than a verified ownership link.

[ADVISORY] The 'all menu actions available' test grants AlertingRuleDelete via setFolderAccessControl but asserts only 4 menu items and never asserts the delete menuitem's presence or absence, so the diff's silent removal of Delete from the list-view rule menu ships unverified either way. If Delete was supposed to remain available in the list view (the permission is explicitly granted in the test), the test bakes in its absence without anyone deciding so; a future regression or an intentional-but-wrong removal of silence/duplicate/export would equally pass as long as the count is 4, because the assertions check individual items only for the happy path and a bare count for everything else.

[ADVISORY] The plural-hook mocks (useRulerRuleAbilities, useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities) hand-copy the per-action logic already written for the singular hooks, so every RBAC scenario is duplicated across two mock implementations that must be kept in sync by hand. If AlertRuleMenu switches which hook family it consumes (exactly what this diff did once already, per the deleted comment about useRulerRuleAbility vs useAlertRuleAbility), the stale duplicate mock keeps the tests green while the real permission logic regresses — the file already documents one instance of this drift in its own comments.

[ADVISORY] The recording-rule and unknown-rule branches of the new GrafanaRuleListItem component have no test triggering them; GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx (the only test file exercising this component) builds every fixture from grafanaRulerGroup, which is an alerting rule. A regression in the RecordingRuleListItem rendering path (e.g. passing alerting-only props like state/instancesCount into the wrong branch, or misclassifying recording rules into UnknownRuleListItem) renders broken list rows for recording rules with the suite still passing.

[ADVISORY] The test renamed from 'creating state when only ruler rule exists' to 'More button with action menu options' now sets up the all-rules-present scenario, leaving the deleted Creating/Deleting transitional states with zero replacement coverage even though the components that rendered them (RuleOperationListItem paths in GrafanaGroupLoader) were removed in this same diff. The deletion of the Creating/Deleting UI is a user-visible behavioral change (rules mid-create/mid-delete no longer render as such) that no test in the diff pins down; the check that the renamed test does perform (aria-label 'More' and textContent 'More') is low-value attribute mirroring that would pass even if the transitional-state removal broke rendering of the rule row itself.

[BUG] GrafanaGroupLoader now renders only rules present in the Prometheus response, so rules mid-propagation (present only in the Ruler = 'Creating', or present only in Prometheus = 'Deleting') are silently omitted from the list instead of being shown with their operation state. A user who deletes a Grafana-managed rule sees it disappear instantly from the list while the Prometheus-side delete has not propagated; if propagation fails or lags the rule reappears on the next poll with no 'Deleting' indication, and a newly created rule is invisible until Prometheus catches up — the UI reports a partial/incorrect list as if it were complete, with no error or status surfaced.

[ADVISORY] Deleting matchRules also deletes the only diagnostic (logWarning 'Grafana Managed Rules: No matching Prometheus rule found for Ruler rule') that surfaced ruler/prometheus eventual-consistency mismatches, and the diff introduces no replacement telemetry for the now-unmatched rule paths. When the strong-consistency assumption behind removing the matching logic is violated (a real state the old code explicitly logged), operators lose the signal entirely — the divergence is invisible in both UI and analytics, making the resulting confusing list behavior undiagnosable.

[BUG] For non-Grafana (cloud/Mimir) rules rendered from the list view, useGrafanaPromRuleAbility is passed skipToken and useRulerRuleAbility is called with an undefined rulerRule (the list view no longer fetches ruler data), so both ability paths resolve false and all edit/delete actions are hidden for cloud rules. Cloud datasource rules lose their Edit/Delete buttons in the alert list: the user with valid permissions sees a rule with no available actions and no error explaining why, a silent permission-computation regression rather than an explicit 'unsupported' state.

[BUG] In useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, `MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable && isAlertingRule` evaluates an array's truthiness (arrays are always truthy), so the supported flag for Pause, Restore and DeletePermanently collapses to just `isAlertingRule`, dropping both the immutable-rule guard and the loading guard. Provisioned Grafana rules report Pause/Restore/DeletePermanently as supported (instead of unsupported), so those menu items render as enabled-but-blocked or visible-when-they-should-be-hidden, and during folder-permission loading the supported flag is already true instead of 'not supported while loading' — the guard the MaybeSupported mechanism exists to provide is silently bypassed for these three actions.

[ADVISORY] useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable treats a failed folder fetch identically to 'no permission': when the useFolder query errors, folder stays undefined and the hook returns isEditable/isRemovable false with no error surfaced. A user with full edit permissions whose folder metadata request fails permanently sees all edit/delete/silence actions silently disappear from the rule menu; the transient failure is indistinguishable from an access-control denial and nothing tells the user or developer that the permission check itself could not be evaluated.

[ADVISORY] After `prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` has already narrowed the rule, the line `const promAlertingRule = rule && rule.type === PromRuleType.Alerting ? rule : undefined;` re-checks truthiness and type redundantly, keeping two overlapping predicates for the same condition. The next change to the alerting-vs-recording dispatch has to keep two predicates in sync; if they drift (e.g. the type guard is broadened but this line is not), instancesCount and state will be silently computed against undefined while the item still renders as an alerting rule.

Also, the refactor removes dependence on the ruler DTO in the list view (`GrafanaGroupLoader` now renders only from `promResponse`), so the old fallback `rule?.isPaused ?? is_paused` is no longer applicable in the new data flow. Whether the Prometheus endpoint populates `isPaused` correctly cannot be verified from this diff alone.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the ruler-side query and the `matchRules` logic from `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx` and now renders only `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules` as `GrafanaRuleListItem`s. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] A custom `skipToken` Symbol is exported from useAbilities.ts, shadowing RTK Query's well-known skipToken concept with a different mechanism (undefined-swapping) inside the same codebase The next contributor will import skipToken from @reduxjs/toolkit/query (the conventional source) and pass it to these hooks; the hooks only check `rule === skipToken` against this local Symbol, so a foreign skipToken is treated as a real undefined rule by coincidence but any future hook checking token identity diverges — two 'skip' conventions coexist

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] RuleActionsButtons.V2 silently ORs ruler and grafana-prom edit abilities and additionally returns null (rendering nothing, including the delete/silence buttons previously available) whenever neither rulerRule nor a grafana promRule is provided For non-Grafana prom-only rules the component logs a warning and renders no action buttons at all, changing behavior for any existing caller that previously passed only promRule; the logWarning fires per rule row on the list page, generating warning noise at list scale

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] useAllRulerRuleAbilities hardcodes isFederated = false (with a TODO), so federated rule groups are no longer treated as immutable and Pause/Delete/Update are offered for rules the previous code locked down. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable calls useFolder(folderUID) for every GrafanaPromRuleDTO it is invoked on, and useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities is invoked per rule via useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities in AlertRuleMenu for every list row — an N+1 folder-fetch pattern on the rule list hot path. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] isPaused is now sourced only from rule?.isPaused, dropping the ruler-rule fallback (rule?.isPaused ?? is_paused) the deleted GrafanaRuleLoader used. If the Grafana prom rules endpoint does not populate isPaused for a paused rule (the field was previously sourced from the ruler DTO's grafana_alert.is_paused), paused rules render as unpaused in the list — a displayed-state mismatch versus the rule's real state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Every ability is computed as rulerAbility OR grafanaPromAbility, creating two parallel permission-evaluation paths whose result is the union of their grants. Any future divergence between the ruler-side checks (useAllRulerRuleAbilities) and the prom-side checks (useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities — different helpers like useCanSilenceInFolder vs useCanSilence, getRulesPermissions('grafana') hardcoded) silently widens permissions to the more permissive path; the staff-level shape here is a single ability source per rule type, not an OR of two.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces two parallel ability-evaluation paths and unions them via OR. In AlertRuleMenu.tsx, each `canX` is computed as `(rulerSupported && rulerAllowed) || (grafanaSupported && grafanaAllowed)` after calling both `useRulerRuleAbilities(...)` and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(..., actions)` (with `skipToken` only gating the prom path for non-Grafana prom rules). Similarly, RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx computes `canEditRule` as an OR between `useRulerRuleAbility(...)` and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility(...)`. The new prom-side ability implementation (`useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`) uses different logic than ruler-side (`useAllRulerRuleAbilities`): e.g., hardcoded `getRulesPermissions('grafana')`, `useCanSilenceInFolder(rule?.folderUid)` + `useGrafanaRulesSilenceSupport()` vs `useCanSilence(rule)`, and different support assumptions (`AlwaysSupported` vs ruler availability). This is a concrete, diff-grounded architectural/security-risk concern: if these paths diverge, the OR will pick the more permissive result. It’s not a currently provable defect from the diff alone, but it is a specific design issue introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getIsProvisioned for the prom-rule path now depends on isProvisionedPromRule(promRule) reading provenance from the prom rules endpoint, replacing the previous ruler-side grafana_alert.provenance check — a single-source-of-truth swap with no verification the prom endpoint carries the field. If GrafanaPromRuleDTO omits or under-populates provenance (it was authoritative on the ruler DTO), provisioned rules are detected as unprovisioned and rendered editable — the exact immutability the provisioned check exists to protect.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does switch provisioned detection for the prom-rule-only path to `isProvisionedPromRule(promRule)` (RuleActionsButtons.V2 `getIsProvisioned`), which relies on `promRule.provenance` (`utils/rules.ts`). While the type `GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase` was updated to include an optional `provenance?: string`, the diff does not show any runtime guarantee that the Prom rules endpoint actually populates this field (it’s optional and no fallback to the former ruler-side `grafana_alert.provenance` exists when only a prom rule is available). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] useAllAlertRuleAbilities was silently re-pointed from getRulesSourceName(rule.namespace.rulesSource) to getGroupOriginName(groupIdentifier.fromCombinedRule(rule)) while keeping its public signature, changing which data source name drives permission checks for existing callers. Out-of-tree or unmodified in-tree callers of the still-exported useAllAlertRuleAbilities now compute permissions from the group-origin name instead of the namespace's rules source; for non-grafana sources this can flip permission results, and the change is invisible at the call site because the hook signature is unchanged.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `useAllAlertRuleAbilities(rule: CombinedRule)` keeping the same public signature but changing its internal routing: it now builds `groupIdentifierV2 = groupIdentifier.fromCombinedRule(rule)` and delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule.rulerRule, groupIdentifierV2)`. `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` computes `rulesSourceName` via `getGroupOriginName(groupIdentifier)` (and the previous `getRulesSourceName(rule.namespace.rulesSource)` logic was removed from `useAllAlertRuleAbilities`). This is a behavior change for existing callers that is invisible at the call site, and it could affect permission checks depending on how those two “source name” derivations differ. However, the diff alone does not prove the new behavior is incorrect in practice (it may be an intended refactor), so it’s best classified as a real compatibility/architecture concern rather than a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The refactor changes permission semantics from 'AND of ruler ability' to 'OR of ruler ability and grafana-prom ability' (canPause = (ruler && ruler) || (grafana && grafana)) without the component's consumers or the stated intent acknowledging the loosening. A rule that the ruler API says is unsupported but the prom path reports as allowed now shows actions that previously were hidden — e.g. plugin-provided or provisioned rules handled differently by the two ability paths may become editable/deletable in the menu, expanding what users can attempt beyond the original intent.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce the exact semantic change described: in AlertRuleMenu.tsx, each `canX` is now computed as `(rulerSupported && rulerAllowed) || (grafanaSupported && grafanaAllowed)` after adding `useRulerRuleAbilities` and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`. Previously it was only the ruler ability (`useRulerRuleAbility`). The same OR-merge is also applied in RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx for edit (`canEditRule`). The intent comment mentions list view no longer calling the ruler API, but the code applies OR unconditionally for Grafana rules, and the two ability implementations are visibly different (e.g., `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` uses `MaybeSupported = AlwaysSupported` and different immutability checks based on `GrafanaPromRuleDTO`), so a mismatch could make actions appear in cases where the ruler-based path would have hidden them. The finding’s specific examples (plugin-provided/provisioned mismatches) aren’t fully provable from this diff alone (depends on how `isPluginProvidedRule` works for prom DTOs), but the loosening/behavior change itself is directly grounded in the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Authorization for edit is now the logical OR of two independently computed ability checks (ruler-based and promRule-based), so an action is offered whenever either path grants it rather than when the authoritative path does. The union composition is fail-open: whichever hook has the more permissive semantics wins. For Grafana-managed rules rendered from the list view (rule === undefined, promRule set), the promRule path in useAbilities.ts now hardcodes MaybeSupported = AlwaysSupported and checks only folder metadata permissions, dropping the ruler-availability and loading gating the ruler path enforced; a user whose folder metadata grants update but who is denied by any server-side rule-level condition the old path covered is shown an Edit/Delete button whose action the backend then rejects — UI-exposed authorization decided by the weaker of two checks rather than the server's actual policy.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change authorization/UI gating to a logical OR of two ability sources. In `AlertRuleMenu.tsx`, `canPause/canDelete/...` are now computed as `(rulerSupported && rulerAllowed) || (grafanaSupported && grafanaAllowed)`. In `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx`, `canEditRule` is similarly OR’d between `useRulerRuleAbility` and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility`. Also, the new `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` in `useAbilities.ts` sets `MaybeSupported` to `AlwaysSupported` (except while folder is loading), and it no longer uses the `isRulerAvailable` gating present in `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`. That creates a real, diff-grounded concern about diverging/possibly weaker UI gating depending on which hook is used. However, the finding’s claim that this definitively results in backend-rejected actions (or that the ruler-based path is the authoritative policy) cannot be verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities replaces the loading/isRulerAvailable support gate with unconditional AlwaysSupported, so Delete, Pause, Duplicate and Restore become 'supported' for every Grafana prom rule as soon as loading completes. Menu action availability (the [supported, allowed] pair) is no longer derived from any capability signal, only from folder metadata permissions; combined with the OR-union in AlertRuleMenu/RuleActionsButtons.V2 this means action buttons are rendered purely on client-side permission metadata for rules the ruler path would have marked unsupported, exposing mutation entry points (delete modal, clone flow, silence drawer) to users the previous gating hid — server enforcement is the only remaining barrier.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a real change in the “supported” side of abilities for Grafana Prom rules: in `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` `MaybeSupported` becomes `loading ? NotSupported : AlwaysSupported` (and `getRulesPermissions('grafana')` + folder metadata drive `allowed`), whereas the older ruler-based path gated support on `isRulerAvailable`. Also, `AlertRuleMenu.tsx` and `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx` now OR-union ruler abilities with Grafana Prom abilities, so a rule can be treated as supported/allowed via the Prom path even if the ruler path would return unsupported. However, whether this is an actual defect/security issue (i.e., actions truly unsupported server-side) is not verifiable from the diff alone; it may be an intentional UX change given the explicit removal of ruler API requests in list view.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable authorizes edit/delete purely from the folderUid string carried in the API-returned GrafanaPromRuleDTO via ctx.hasPermissionInMetadata, with no validation that the rule actually resides in that folder. The permission decision is keyed on a server-supplied field that the diff treats as trusted input; any path that lets a rule be rendered with a mismatched or attacker-influenced folderUid (e.g. cross-folder rule rendering in the new list view) causes the folder's permission metadata to be evaluated for the wrong folder, granting edit/delete UI for a rule outside the user's authorized folder — the server rejects the write, but the authorization model now depends on an unscoped, response-controlled identifier rather than a verified ownership link.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable()` which derives edit/delete capability from `rule.folderUid` (from `GrafanaPromRuleDTO`) by calling `useFolder(folderUID)` and then `ctx.hasPermissionInMetadata(...)` on that folder’s metadata. There is no check that `rule.folderUid` matches the folder/group context the rule is rendered under (e.g., `groupIdentifier.namespace.uid` passed around in list components), so a mismatched `folderUid` in the rendered rule object could cause the UI to evaluate permissions against the wrong folder and show Edit/Delete incorrectly. This is a real, diff-grounded design/authorization-model concern for UI gating, though server-side enforcement would still prevent unauthorized writes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The 'all menu actions available' test grants AlertingRuleDelete via setFolderAccessControl but asserts only 4 menu items and never asserts the delete menuitem's presence or absence, so the diff's silent removal of Delete from the list-view rule menu ships unverified either way. If Delete was supposed to remain available in the list view (the permission is explicitly granted in the test), the test bakes in its absence without anyone deciding so; a future regression or an intentional-but-wrong removal of silence/duplicate/export would equally pass as long as the count is 4, because the assertions check individual items only for the happy path and a bare count for everything else.

adjudication.rationale: In GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx, the shared beforeEach grants AlertingRuleDelete via grantUserPermissions and setFolderAccessControl, and the UI helper even defines a delete menuitem selector, but the "should render correct menu actions when More button is clicked" test only asserts Silence/Copy link/Duplicate/Export and then asserts menuitem count === 4 without explicitly asserting whether Delete should be present or absent. This is a test/spec clarity gap around delete behavior in the list-view menu introduced/updated by this diff, not a directly verifiable runtime bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The plural-hook mocks (useRulerRuleAbilities, useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities) hand-copy the per-action logic already written for the singular hooks, so every RBAC scenario is duplicated across two mock implementations that must be kept in sync by hand. If AlertRuleMenu switches which hook family it consumes (exactly what this diff did once already, per the deleted comment about useRulerRuleAbility vs useAlertRuleAbility), the stale duplicate mock keeps the tests green while the real permission logic regresses — the file already documents one instance of this drift in its own comments.

adjudication.rationale: In `RulesTable.test.tsx`, the test suite now mocks both singular and plural ability hooks (`useAlertRuleAbility`/`useRulerRuleAbility`/`useGrafanaPromRuleAbility` and also `useRulerRuleAbilities`/`useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`). Several RBAC scenarios re-encode the same per-action permission logic in more than one mock (e.g., Grafana rule tests set `useAlertRuleAbility` and separately implement `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` with the same action-based branching). This is a diff-grounded maintainability/testing-architecture issue: if components change which hook they consume, duplicated mocks can diverge and mask regressions. It’s not a runtime defect, but it weakens test reliability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The recording-rule and unknown-rule branches of the new GrafanaRuleListItem component have no test triggering them; GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx (the only test file exercising this component) builds every fixture from grafanaRulerGroup, which is an alerting rule. A regression in the RecordingRuleListItem rendering path (e.g. passing alerting-only props like state/instancesCount into the wrong branch, or misclassifying recording rules into UnknownRuleListItem) renders broken list rows for recording rules with the suite still passing.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new component `GrafanaRuleListItem` with three rendering branches: alerting (`prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule`), recording (`prometheusRuleType.grafana.recordingRule`), and fallback to `UnknownRuleListItem`. The only added/modified test that exercises this component is `GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx`, and all its fixtures come from `grafanaRulerGroup` converted via `rulerGroupToPromGroup(...)`, with assertions keyed off `rule.grafana_alert.title` and alerting-only menu items (e.g., Silence). Nothing in the shown tests constructs a `GrafanaPromRuleDTO` recording rule or an unclassified rule, so the `RecordingRuleListItem` and `UnknownRuleListItem` branches in `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx` are untested, making regressions in rule-type classification/rendering plausibly undetected.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The test renamed from 'creating state when only ruler rule exists' to 'More button with action menu options' now sets up the all-rules-present scenario, leaving the deleted Creating/Deleting transitional states with zero replacement coverage even though the components that rendered them (RuleOperationListItem paths in GrafanaGroupLoader) were removed in this same diff. The deletion of the Creating/Deleting UI is a user-visible behavioral change (rules mid-create/mid-delete no longer render as such) that no test in the diff pins down; the check that the renamed test does perform (aria-label 'More' and textContent 'More') is low-value attribute mirroring that would pass even if the transitional-state removal broke rendering of the rule row itself.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the Creating/Deleting transitional-state rendering paths in `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx` (deleted ruler API query, deleted `matchRules`, deleted `RuleOperationListItem` rendering for `promOnlyRules`, and deleted the `Creating` branch when a ruler rule lacks a matching prom rule). Correspondingly, `GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx` deletes the prior tests that covered those states ("creating state when only ruler rule exists" and "delete rule operation list item when only prom rule exists") and replaces them with tests focused on the presence/attributes of the "More" button and menu items. This is a user-visible behavioral change whose removal is no longer pinned by tests in this diff; that’s a specific, diff-grounded test-coverage concern, not a verifiable functional bug by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] GrafanaGroupLoader now renders only rules present in the Prometheus response, so rules mid-propagation (present only in the Ruler = 'Creating', or present only in Prometheus = 'Deleting') are silently omitted from the list instead of being shown with their operation state. A user who deletes a Grafana-managed rule sees it disappear instantly from the list while the Prometheus-side delete has not propagated; if propagation fails or lags the rule reappears on the next poll with no 'Deleting' indication, and a newly created rule is invisible until Prometheus catches up — the UI reports a partial/incorrect list as if it were complete, with no error or status surfaced.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a clear behavior change: `GrafanaGroupLoader` no longer queries the Ruler API nor reconciles Ruler vs Prom rules (`useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery`, `matchRules`, and `RuleOperationListItem` were removed), and now renders only `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules` (GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx). This means any rule that exists only on the Ruler side cannot be rendered (previously shown as `RuleOperation.Creating`), and Prom-only rules are no longer shown with a `Deleting` operation indicator (they’ll render as normal `GrafanaRuleListItem`). However, the finding’s claim that Prom-only (“Deleting”) rules are "silently omitted" is not supported by the new code, since Prom rules are exactly what is rendered; the regression is loss of operation-state signaling and inability to show ruler-only rules, contingent on such inconsistency still being possible.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Deleting matchRules also deletes the only diagnostic (logWarning 'Grafana Managed Rules: No matching Prometheus rule found for Ruler rule') that surfaced ruler/prometheus eventual-consistency mismatches, and the diff introduces no replacement telemetry for the now-unmatched rule paths. When the strong-consistency assumption behind removing the matching logic is violated (a real state the old code explicitly logged), operators lose the signal entirely — the divergence is invisible in both UI and analytics, making the resulting confusing list behavior undiagnosable.

adjudication.rationale: The diff deletes `matchRules()` from `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx`, including the only explicit diagnostic `logWarning('Grafana Managed Rules: No matching Prometheus rule found for Ruler rule', ...)` that fired when `promOnlyRules.length > 0`. The refactor also removes the Ruler query entirely (`useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery` and related logic), so the component no longer has any mechanism to detect or log ruler↔prom divergence, and no replacement telemetry/logging is introduced elsewhere in the shown changes. This is a concrete, diff-grounded observability/regression concern, but it is not strictly a verifiable functional defect given the new “strong consistency” assumption.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] For non-Grafana (cloud/Mimir) rules rendered from the list view, useGrafanaPromRuleAbility is passed skipToken and useRulerRuleAbility is called with an undefined rulerRule (the list view no longer fetches ruler data), so both ability paths resolve false and all edit/delete actions are hidden for cloud rules. Cloud datasource rules lose their Edit/Delete buttons in the alert list: the user with valid permissions sees a rule with no available actions and no error explaining why, a silent permission-computation regression rather than an explicit 'unsupported' state.

adjudication.rationale: The diff only removes ruler-API fetching for *Grafana-managed* rules (e.g., `GrafanaGroupLoader` drops `useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery` and `prometheusGroupsGenerator` removes prefetching `getGrafanaRulerGroup`). It does not show that cloud/Mimir (non-Grafana) rules in the list view stop providing `rulerRule` data. In `AlertRuleMenu`, the ruler-based path is explicitly updated to tolerate `rulerRule` being `undefined` (`useRulerRuleAbilities(rule: RulerRuleDTO | undefined, ...)`), and the Grafana-prom path is gated to Grafana prom rules only (`prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule) ? promRule : skipToken`). So the claimed regression specifically for cloud/Mimir rules (“both paths resolve false so actions are hidden”) is not verifiable from this diff because the prerequisite—cloud rules being rendered without `rulerRule`—is not demonstrated here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, `MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable && isAlertingRule` evaluates an array's truthiness (arrays are always truthy), so the supported flag for Pause, Restore and DeletePermanently collapses to just `isAlertingRule`, dropping both the immutable-rule guard and the loading guard. Provisioned Grafana rules report Pause/Restore/DeletePermanently as supported (instead of unsupported), so those menu items render as enabled-but-blocked or visible-when-they-should-be-hidden, and during folder-permission loading the supported flag is already true instead of 'not supported while loading' — the guard the MaybeSupported mechanism exists to provide is silently bypassed for these three actions.

adjudication.rationale: In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, `MaybeSupported`, `NotSupported`, and `AlwaysSupported` are used as boolean “supported” flags (consistent with their use in `toAbility(AlwaysSupported, ...)` elsewhere in the same diff). `MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable` is therefore also a boolean, not an ability tuple/array, so `MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable && isAlertingRule` does not evaluate an array’s truthiness. The immutable-rule and loading guards are not bypassed for Pause/Restore/DeletePermanently based on what the diff shows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable treats a failed folder fetch identically to 'no permission': when the useFolder query errors, folder stays undefined and the hook returns isEditable/isRemovable false with no error surfaced. A user with full edit permissions whose folder metadata request fails permanently sees all edit/delete/silence actions silently disappear from the rule menu; the transient failure is indistinguishable from an access-control denial and nothing tells the user or developer that the permission check itself could not be evaluated.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable` which calls `useFolder(folderUID)` but does not handle any error state—only `{ folder, loading }` is read. When `folderUID` is set and `folder` is falsy, it returns `{ isEditable: false, isRemovable: false, loading }` without surfacing that evaluation failed. If `useFolder` results in `folder === undefined` due to a request error (not just "still loading"), the hook will treat that identically to "no permission" and downstream abilities (e.g. in `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`) will hide edit/delete/silence actions with no indication of failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] After `prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` has already narrowed the rule, the line `const promAlertingRule = rule && rule.type === PromRuleType.Alerting ? rule : undefined;` re-checks truthiness and type redundantly, keeping two overlapping predicates for the same condition. The next change to the alerting-vs-recording dispatch has to keep two predicates in sync; if they drift (e.g. the type guard is broadened but this line is not), instancesCount and state will be silently computed against undefined while the item still renders as an alerting rule.

adjudication.rationale: In `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx`, there is indeed a second check `rule && rule.type === PromRuleType.Alerting ? rule : undefined` inside the branch guarded by `prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`. However, the diff does not show the implementation of `prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule`, so we cannot verify that it already guarantees `rule.type === PromRuleType.Alerting` (i.e., that the second check is redundant) or that predicate drift is a realistic risk introduced by this PR. As stated, the finding depends on behavior not present in the diff and is primarily a maintainability/style concern rather than a verifiable defect.
